From 3c29b6038828c1f4c9ecbfec14d4fc5e25f1c947 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2017 11:37:01 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/8xx: fix mpc8xx_get_irq() return on no irq

IRQ 0 is a valid HW interrupt. So get_irq() shall return 0 when
there is no irq, instead of returning irq_linear_revmap(... ,0)

Fixes: f2a0bd3753dad ("[POWERPC] 8xx: powerpc port of core CPM PIC")
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c b/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c
index 3e828b20c21e..2842f9d63d21 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ unsigned int mpc8xx_get_irq(void)
 	irq = in_be32(&siu_reg->sc_sivec) >> 26;
 
 	if (irq == PIC_VEC_SPURRIOUS)
-		irq = 0;
+		return 0;
 
         return irq_linear_revmap(mpc8xx_pic_host, irq);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c`**
- The function `mpc8xx_get_irq()` was modified to change the return behavior when a spurious interrupt is detected. 
- The line that previously set `irq` to 0 when a spurious interrupt was detected has been replaced with a direct return of 0. This means that instead of continuing to process and returning a value from `irq_linear_revmap`, the function will now immediately return 0 when there is no valid interrupt.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug where the function incorrectly returned a value from `irq_linear_revmap` when no valid interrupt was present (specifically when a spurious interrupt occurred). The change ensures that the function correctly indicates the absence of an interrupt by returning 0, which is a valid hardware interrupt in this context. This fix is linked to a previous commit that introduced the issue, as indicated by the "Fixes" tag in the patch.

powerpc/8xx: fix mpc8xx_get_irq() return on no irq

there is no irq, instead of returning irq_linear_revmap(... ,0)

Fixes: f2a0bd3753dad ("[POWERPC] 8xx: powerpc port of core CPM PIC")
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `mpc8xx_get_irq()` function returning a value from `irq_linear_revmap` even when there was no valid interrupt, specifically in the case of a spurious interrupt. This led to incorrect handling of IRQ 0, which is a valid hardware interrupt, instead of correctly indicating the absence of an interrupt by returning 0.

Here is the patch:
 
 unsigned int mpc8xx_get_irq(void)
 {
 	int irq;
 
 	/* For MPC8xx, read the SIVEC register and shift the bits down
 	 * to get the irq number.
 	 */
 	irq = in_be32(&siu_reg->sc_sivec) >> 26;
 
 	if (irq == PIC_VEC_SPURRIOUS)
-		irq = 0;
+		return 0;
 
         return irq_linear_revmap(mpc8xx_pic_host, irq);
 
 }

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
irq = in_be32(&siu_reg->sc_sivec) >> 26;
if (irq == PIC_VEC_SPURRIOUS)
    irq = 0;
```
Reason:
The function `mpc8xx_get_irq()` reads the interrupt vector and checks if it corresponds to a spurious interrupt. If it does, it sets `irq` to 0, but then it proceeds to return the result of `irq_linear_revmap(mpc8xx_pic_host, irq)`, which can incorrectly map IRQ 0 to a valid interrupt instead of indicating that there is no interrupt.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (irq == PIC_VEC_SPURRIOUS)
    return 0;
```
Reason:
The patch modifies the handling of spurious interrupts by returning 0 immediately when a spurious interrupt is detected. This ensures that the function correctly indicates the absence of an interrupt (returning 0) instead of potentially returning an incorrect mapping from `irq_linear_revmap`, thus properly handling IRQ 0 as a valid hardware interrupt.
